subject: Request: compact telemetry snapshot for commitment assessment
messages:
From: Claire Zhou <claire.zhou@orbitx.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: ops@orbitx.com
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sizing input: compact telemetry snapshot request

Hi Markus —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We’re moving fast toward a committed Reserved/Dedicated path and procurement asked for a short telemetry artifact so your pre-sales engineering can validate the commit size. Can you confirm the data points your team needs?

Quick context: OrbitX is planning an initial 3-month Dedicated pilot behind our product search API. Typical traffic is highly spiky around marketing drops; average QPS is low but burst P99 is what drives our decisions. We attach a small CSV with 7 days of anonymized request-level telemetry and a PNG with a histogram we generated.

Attachments: orbitx_telemetry_sample_202607.csv (CSV, ~120KB), prompt_response_histogram.png (PNG, ~45KB)

Top asks from procurement:
- A short write-up mapping their burst profile to a recommended starting GPU mix and a min-burst floor for SLA guarantees.
- Confirmation of what telemetry fields are sufficient (seq length, response tokens, latency, session_id).
- Estimated KV-cache footprint for typical sessions (approx counts ok).

Can you or someone on your sizing team take a look today or tomorrow? We’d like a decision to feed into the executive approval on Mon.

– Claire
Claire Zhou
Head of Platform Operations, OrbitX
claire.zhou@orbitx.com
From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: Claire Zhou <claire.zhou@orbitx.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing input: compact telemetry snapshot request

Claire —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the sample CSV. To make the intake compact and actionable for a commit recommendation we typically need:
- per-request: timestamp (ISO), route/api, prompt_token_count, response_token_count, tail_latency_ms (P50/P95/P99 if present), session_id (hashed).
- daily aggregates: peak-minute QPS, 95th/99th prompt+response length percentiles, burst duration distribution.
- a small sample of long-tail prompts (we don’t need full text; a trimmed token-count histogram + example prompt categories is fine).

If you can add a tiny table (or column) with an anonymized session affinity indicator (true/false) that helps with session pool sizing. Otherwise this CSV looks usable. I’ve uploaded our compact intake worksheet here: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aBcD_example — please drop the CSV into Tab A and fill the burst-note column if possible.

We’ll run an initial mapping and get back with a conservative starting GPU mix (model sizes and counts), plus an estimated KV cache footprint. Kar thik will lead the mapping — looping him in.

I’ll schedule a 45-min workshop for Fri to walk through assumptions unless you prefer a short async first pass.

Thanks,
Markus
Markus Klein
Senior Solutions Architect — Dedicated Inference
Redwood Inference

To: markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: ops@orbitx.com
Date: Fri, 7 Aug 2026 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing input: compact telemetry snapshot request

On Wed, Aug 5, 2026 at 10:03 AM markus_klein@redwood.com wrote:
> Claire —
>
> Appreciate the quick turnaround and the sample CSV. To make the intake compact and actionable for a commit recommendation we typically need:
> - per-request: timestamp (ISO), route/api, prompt_token_count, response_token_count, tail_latency_ms (P50/P95/P99 if present), session_id (hashed).
> - daily aggregates: peak-minute QPS, 95th/99th prompt+response length percentiles, burst duration distribution.
> - a small sample of long-tail prompts (we don’t need full text; a trimmed token-count histogram + example prompt categories is fine).

Thanks Markus — I added the session_affinity column and a short sheet with per-minute peak QPS aggregates. Also attached a quick KV-cache estimate we ran internally (orbitx_kv_cache_estimate.xlsx).

Attachments: orbitx_kv_cache_estimate.xlsx (XLSX, ~85KB)

A few clarifications from our side:
- The pilot will primarily hit a 16k context vector model for embeddings+rerank; generation calls use a 4k context LLM at 1:1 traffic ratio.
- Burst windows typically last 3–8 minutes; sustained high QPS beyond 10 minutes is rare.
- We can provide a small set of redacted prompt categories if that helps.

Please let me know if the worksheet is sufficient and whether you want the Fri workshop.

– Claire
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: markus_klein@redwood.com, Claire Zhou <claire.zhou@orbitx.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 7 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing input: compact telemetry snapshot request

Thanks for the sample, Claire — I pulled it into the intake worksheet and did a first-pass decomposition. Quick notes (keeps short so we can discuss on the call):

- Candidate starting fleet (conservative): 2x A100-40GB for the 16k context embedding+rerank cluster (batched inference + caching) and 3x A100-80GB for the 4k generation cluster to keep p99 latency under 500ms during 5-minute bursts.
- KV cache: sample suggests ~1.2M session-keys peak (estimate) with an average k-v payload of ~7KB => ~9GB compressed cache; plan for 16–24GB allocated across pool to allow headroom.
- Batching: we expect continuous batching to reduce token cost by ~18% for the generation path given the prompt/response distribution you provided.

Open questions:
1) Do you expect many concurrent long-lived sessions (websocket-type) or is traffic mostly stateless REST?
2) Are you comfortable with a canary route that fails over to a lower-capacity model variant during extreme spikes?

If answers are quick, I can finalize a short note we can share with procurement that maps to a commitment band and associated monthly seat/commit costs.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Pre-Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: Claire Zhou <claire.zhou@orbitx.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 7 Aug 2026 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing input: compact telemetry snapshot request

Claire —

This is helpful, thank you. Next steps:
1) We’ll convert Karthik’s first-pass into a 1-page commitment recommendation (GPU SKUs, counts, and a conservative burst floor) and a short runbook for burst handling. Expect that in your inbox by EOD Mon.
2) Let’s hold the 45-min workshop as scheduled Friday next week to walk through the assumptions and procurement story — I’ll send the invite shortly.
3) If procurement needs a formal appendix for DocuSign (SLA targets and fallback routing language), Marissa will prepare that template.

Attachments referenced in-thread: orbitx_telemetry_sample_202607.csv, prompt_response_histogram.png, orbitx_kv_cache_estimate.xlsx

If you prefer a smaller async note first, say so — otherwise we’ll proceed with the workshop cadence.

Best,
Markus
